Dee is invented. This is the product we're building.

9:10 AM

A video, shared from the sofa.

Saturday. Dee shares a video to True Convo from the phone: a man saying he makes £800 a month restoring old lamps. By the time Dee's at the Mac it's transcribed, the steps are pulled out, and the claims are marked as claims.

9:20 AM

Known, guessed, claimed. Kept apart.

The PA separates what the video shows (the steps, the tools) from what it claims (the £800) and from what it guessed (what Dee would need). Nothing is dressed up.

9:30 AM

Talk it through. Not a plan yet.

Dee is thinking aloud. The PA doesn't hand it off or write a business plan; it asks three questions and listens.

Inbox · video, 11:40Transcribed. The steps: find lamps at car boots, rewire, new shade, list online. His claim: £800 a month. He doesn't say how many hours or what he spends.

Could I actually do this?

Your PAMaybe. Three questions first. How many hours a week do you honestly have? Have you ever rewired anything? And what would make you stop, if it isn't working?

Six hours. No. Losing more than £150.

9:00 PM

What it cost, honestly.

A Saturday and £135. One practice lamp tomorrow, three listed next week. The PA writes the day down in the Atlas, with the stop line next to it, and sets the 30-day revisit.

9:10 PM

If it doesn't work.

Dee keeps the tools, the skill and the tracker, and the stop line says when to stop. Nothing is lost but a Saturday. The PA won't nag Dee to keep going.

9:20 PM

If it does.

The same page, ledger, tracker and PA scale with it. Nothing to migrate, nothing to subscribe to. A bigger brain is an option, never the floor.

What an idea costs, here.

A Saturday and a Mac you own. No subscription, no account, no card. A model on the machine you already have.
A stop line, written down. The PA keeps the line Dee set and says plainly when it's crossed. It never nags you to keep going.
Claims stay claims. The video's £800 is marked as his claim, the budget's guesses as guesses. Nothing is dressed up.
Your words, your yes. Listings and pages go up in your words, when you click.
Open core. Copy it, change it, label it as your own.
Leave any time. Export everything in a form that works without us.

Not on your own

More than software.

True Convo is meant to come with people: lessons in plain words, others in the same spot as Dee, and the apps and templates they make and share.

ComingLearn

Short lessons on testing an idea before spending on it, and on spotting a claim in a video.

ComingPeople

People who also started from a video, saying honestly what was true and what wasn't.

ComingShared

Starter plans and trackers shared by people a few months further along.

None of this exists yet. It's what we hope to build with the first people who use True Convo, and we'll say so plainly until it's real.

11:00 PM

A Saturday, £135, and a stop line.

A plan that fits, one skill to learn, a tracker, a page ready to publish, and a date to be honest about it. All on a Mac Dee already owned, which sent nothing anywhere today. No account with us. No ads. Nothing sold on.

Where this stands. True Convo is in development and not out yet. Built so far: the pill, dictation at the cursor, the Desk with a model on the Mac, encrypted storage, and the first engines for lists, habits, tasks, the agenda, mail, the calendar, time, sources and the capture inbox. Being built now: the PA, the iPhone, sync and the first-run guide. The site builder, the ledger and building your own apps come after launch. The lessons, the community and the shared library are a plan too; none of them exist yet. Dee and everything on this page are invented to show the plan; the tests decide the order.
